name: roots-sh
description: The dev tool roots roots.sh and its Jet twin orchestrator/Roots.jet (#5072 c9): a root is what bash sees once it has sourced the machine's ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/jet/env, else the environment's value, else the default derived from $HOME and the XDG directories; the checkout defaults to the one holding the program. Sourced, roots.sh exports the roots; run by bash with root names, it prints `NAME=value` for each, as Roots.jet does, and exits 64 at a name that is not one of its eight (JET_BIN is roots.mjs's alone). Every case sets every root (empty is unset, as both programs read it) so the machine's own leak into nothing, and the XDG data and config directories are relative so no path names the machine. HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME stay the machine's, because the harness starts both programs through Tools/agent/JetEnv.jet, which keeps its dev shells there; check.jet writes the machine's cache directory as `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, its home directory as `<HOME>` and a root that is this checkout as `<checkout>`. fixtures/cfg/jet/env is a machine's env file: quoted and bare values, `export`, a `${NAME:-default}` value that keeps the environment's, a name set twice, and an XDG directory the defaults then derive from. fixtures/quoting/jet/env reads $HOME and an earlier root in double quotes, keeps `$HOME` in single quotes, mixes quotes and escapes in one word, expands `~` at the start and after `:`, uses ${NAME:-word}, ${NAME-word} on an empty name, ${NAME:+word}, ${#NAME}, ${NAME:=word} in a `:` command, $1, `;`, a comment, `+=`, `export` of two names, a line continuation, and assignments before a command, which do not stay. fixtures/failing/jet/env fails a ${NAME:?word}, which ends bash with exit 1. The cases cover the defaults, the environment over the defaults, the env file over the environment and under it, the quoting file, the failing file, the checkout default, a name that is not a root after one that is (JET_ROOT, then JET_BIN), and no name. Commands the file runs, and constructs Roots.jet skips whole (pipelines, lists, redirections, subshells, command substitution, other parameter forms, `~user`), are outside these cases.
